land.text: Arochukwu and the Aro country, taken in the Aro Expedition of 1901-1902

successors.note: The Anglo-Aro War page calls the British side the 'Nigerian Coast Protectorate' and the Royal Niger Company; the entity became the Southern Nigeria Protectorate in 1900 on other pages.

capitals.name: Arochukwu
capitals.note: Infobox capital Arochukwu; the page gives no coordinates, so the dot is approximate (in Abia State).

correction.text: Arochukwu and its neighbourhood, the Aro heartland of the Ibini Ukpabi oracle

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox 'Established: 1640'; the text says 'around the mid-17th century' and 'founded after the end of the Aro-Ibibio Wars' (no date). Abia State (about 6,300 km2) stands for the core; the page gives no area or frontier.

correction.text: the Aro country and its settlements across Igboland: 'Okoro Idozuka ... expanded the state's borders through warfare at the start of the 19th century'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Aro settlements named on the page (Ajalli, Arondizuogu, Ozizza) lie across Igboland; Abia plus the Igboland region (about 40,000 km2) is a stand-in for the trade network and the conquests of the early 19th century. No area on the page; soft.

ledger.note: 1640: the Aro Confederacy is founded at Arochukwu. Infobox 'Established: 1640'; 'it is believed to have been established around the mid-17th century' and 'founded after the end of the Aro-Ibibio Wars' (undated).

region.text: the Igbo hinterland settled and won by the Aro

ledger.note: start of the 19th century: Aro commanders extend the Aro country. 'Later Aro commanders such as Okoro Idozuka ... expanded the state's borders through warfare at the start of the 19th century.' The page names the settlements Ajalli, Arondizuogu and Ozizza, not the conquered peoples.

region.text: the Aro country from the Niger and the coast inland

ledger.note: 1901 (28 November): the British launch the Aro Expedition. 'On November 28, Lt. Col. Arthur Forbes Montanaro led 87 officers, 1,550 soldiers and 2,100 carriers' in four columns from Oguta, Akwete, Unwana and Itu; Arochukwu fell on 28 December 'after four days of fierce battles'.
1902 (March): Aro resistance ends. 'Aro forces were defeated in the last major battle at Bende' in spring 1902; 'Aro dominance crumbled in March 1902'; the infobox gives 'November 1901 - March 1902'.
1902 (March): the Aro country passes to the British. 'By early 1902, the war was over and the Aro Confederacy collapsed' (Aro Confederacy page); Okoro Toti was hanged and Eze Kanu Okoro arrested.

region.text: the Aro Confederacy, to the British protectorate

wars.name: Anglo-Aro War

zones.text: Arochukwu, Bende and the Aro hinterland

wars.outcome: British victory: Arochukwu captured 28 December 1901, last major battle at Bende in spring 1902, Aro dominance gone in March 1902; the Ibini Ukpabi oracle was a target of the plan (the page says the shrine still exists at Arochukwu).
wars.note: Planned 'since September 1899' by Moor and the Royal Niger Company and delayed until November 1901 (Anglo-Aro War page); the Aro Confederacy page has a British attempt to conquer the Aros in 1899 after failed negotiations.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the Aro were a trading network of settlements and an oracle, drawn here as a region.

sources.title: Aro Confederacy
sources.note: Infobox 1640-1902; origins mid-17th century; expansion at the start of the 19th century; 1890s friction with the Royal Niger Company; 1899, 1901 expedition; collapse in early 1902; no area.

sources.title: Anglo-Aro War
sources.note: November 1901 - March 1902; 28 November launch; four axes; Arochukwu 28 December; Bende; Aro dominance crumbled March 1902.

notes: Aro has no Cliopatria row. Two pages opened. The Aro Confederacy page says the Aro-Ibibio Wars preceded the founding but gives no year, so the dossier uses the infobox 1640 (the lead title line reads '(1640-1902)'; two reference titles carry '1690-1720' and '1650-1980' and are not statements of dates). No area figure; the shapes are the Abia State core and Abia plus the Igboland region for the network. The Anglo-Aro War page gives no year for the 28 December capture; 1901 is read from the 28 November launch. The capital dot is approximate. Not placed: Ohafia, Abam, Edda and Ibibio allies and mercenaries; Aro settlements beyond Igboland; the 1899 attempt. Nri is not mentioned on the Aro page. The British side is the Niger Coast Protectorate (the Anglo-Aro page: 'Nigerian Coast Protectorate'; the Southern Nigeria Protectorate from 1900 on other pages), counterpart niger-coast-protectorate.
